chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Tulsa layoff, the Barn and Max Roach's Stravinsky
summary: Layoff in Tulsa where he met Max Roach and J.J. Johnson, jammed at the Barn with Harry Pettiford, and first heard Stravinsky.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Oh, it took a little while. Well, we were all in those long layoffs, you know -- those long layoffs. In fact, the first layoff we had in Tulsa, this is where I first met Max Roach and J.J. Johnson. They were there. About three bands was in town at the time, off. Right? So Joe Albany, a fine pianist, and Porter Kilbert, another very fine alto saxophonist... And Benny had just made "Malibu" and "Poinciana" and those great tracks that he had made with the band.
And all the bands...or about three or four bands was in town. And they had a place called the Barn, where they used

to have dances. So every day, all these musicians would meet up at the Barn and just have like an all-afternoon jam session until the night. It usually ended up with Harry Pettiford, Oscar Pettiford's older brother, he was an alto saxophone player... It usually ended up with everybody sitting around listening to Harry play. He was really fantastic. And I doubt if he ever made a record. But the man, he... He was a heavyset guy, and his alto would sit on his stomach, a la Pete Brown, you know, sitting right on it like a toy set. But he had power and speed! You could just hear him all over the place, you know. And we would end up sitting around listening to him play, all us so-called good young saxophone players.
Benny had a very fine guy who I am quite sure you remember -- Bumps Myers.

Bumps was a fine saxophone player. And we used to meet there... And that's when I first heard Stravinsky's work, "The Firebird Suite" and "Rite of Spring." Max Roach took me around to the hotel. He says, "Look, I want you to hear some things. I want you to hear something." So he took me around to the hotel and put these records on. And that was my first hearing, you know; and that was really exciting.
And we stayed around there, and played dances through Oklahoma, like Oklahoma City and different places, and played at the Army bases and what have you. But that was good experience, you know.
